description: Experimental (`media_buy.execution_requirements`). Details shape a seller that declares `execution_requirements` MUST use for a `VALIDATION_ERROR` returned because a buyer-supplied package does not satisfy an `event_source` or `catalog` entry in its product's `execution_requirements`. Unmet `downstream_connection` requirements use `AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED` with `error-details/authorization-required.json` instead. `error.field` names the first unmet binding; `unmet_requirements[]` lists every unmet requirement found. A seller that also emits `issues[]` SHOULD emit one entry per unmet requirement, in the same order.

field.description: Request path where the resource binds, in the same JSONPath-lite form as `error.field`: `packages[i].optimization_goals` or `packages[i].catalogs` on `create_media_buy`; `new_packages[i].…` or `packages[i].…` on `update_media_buy`. For `not_found` and `ineligible`, sellers SHOULD point at the offending entry (for example `packages[0].optimization_goals[1].event_sources[0]` or `packages[0].catalogs[0]`).

reason.description: `not_bound`: the package does not reference a resource of this kind. `not_found`: the referenced resource is not available to the account (for example an `event_source_id` that was never registered through `sync_event_sources`); register or sync it, then retry. `ineligible`: the referenced resource exists but does not satisfy the requirement (for example an event type or catalog type the requirement does not list).

requirement.description: The product's declared requirement, echoed so the buyer can fix the request without another `get_products` call.

oneOf.description: Each package needs event optimization fed by a conversion event source; declare it only when the product requires event optimization. Satisfied when an `optimization_goals[]` entry of `kind: "event"` that the seller will use has a used `event_sources[]` entry referencing an event source available to the account (registered via `sync_event_sources`, or the seller-managed source it returns under `conversion_tracking.platform_managed: true`) with an `event_type` accepted here.

event_types.description: Event types that satisfy the requirement (any-of): the satisfying `event_sources[]` entry MUST use one of these `event_type` values. Omit when any event type satisfies it.

items.description: Standard marketing event types for event logging, aligned with IAB ECAPI

enumDescriptions.add_to_cart: User added an item to cart
enumDescriptions.add_to_wishlist: User added an item to a wishlist
enumDescriptions.close_convert_lead: Lead converted to a customer or closed deal
enumDescriptions.content_view: User meaningfully consumed a content unit, such as a watch, listen, stream, episode play, or read
enumDescriptions.disqualify_lead: Lead disqualified or marked as not viable
enumDescriptions.follow: User made a free, durable opt-in to an account, channel, feed, list, podcast, or similar owned property
enumDescriptions.lead: User expressed interest (form submission, signup, etc.)
enumDescriptions.qualify_lead: Lead qualified by sales or scoring criteria
enumDescriptions.refund: A purchase was fully or partially refunded (adjusts ROAS)
enumDescriptions.remove_from_cart: User removed an item from cart
enumDescriptions.schedule: User scheduled an appointment or event
enumDescriptions.select_content: User selected or clicked on content (article, video, etc.)
enumDescriptions.select_item: User selected a specific product or item from a list
enumDescriptions.share: User shared content via social or messaging
enumDescriptions.submit_application: User submitted an application (loan, job, etc.)
enumDescriptions.subscribe: User started a paid subscription or paid membership
enumDescriptions.view_content: User viewed specific content (product, article, etc.)
enumDescriptions.watch_milestone: User reached a content progress threshold, such as 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%, or a seconds-viewed milestone

oneOf.description: Each package needs a catalog. Satisfied by a `packages[].catalogs[]` entry whose `type` is in `catalog_types`. App promotion uses `["app"]`; app items carry `app_id`, `bundle_id`, `apple_id`, and `store_url`. Every listed type MUST also appear in the product's `catalog_types`.

catalog_types.description: Catalog types that satisfy the requirement (any-of). One catalog of any listed type satisfies it.

items.description: The type of catalog feed. Determines the item schema and how the platform resolves catalog items. Multiple catalog types can be synced to the same account and referenced together in creatives.

oneOf.title: Catalog Execution Requirement

oneOf.description: The product needs a seller-side platform connection or grant, such as the advertiser account or the publisher identity the ads run as. Satisfied by completing the connection, not by a request field; a missing, pending, expired, or revoked connection fails with `AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED` per `error-details/authorization-required.json`. A connection needed by every package MUST be declared here; one needed only by some formats stays in that format declaration's `required_connections`. With several eligible connected identities, the seller applies its documented default.

allOf.description: A seller/platform-side connection or grant required by a product, format, or request. This is not the AdCP caller credential: the AdCP request is still authenticated once, and the seller uses these stored downstream connections to call a platform or service on the buyer's behalf. Use this shape for platforms that require more than one downstream grant, such as an advertiser account connection plus a publisher identity or post authorization for published-post references.

examples.authorization_instructions: Connect the creator or page that owns the source post.

authorization_instructions.description: Human-readable instructions for completing or restoring this downstream connection.

authorization_url.description: Seller-hosted or provider-hosted URL where a human can complete or restore this downstream connection.

connection_id.description: Seller-defined identifier for an already-created downstream connection. Omit when no connection exists yet or when exposing it would leak platform/account state.

connection_type.description: Kind of downstream connection required. `advertiser_account` is the platform account used to buy/manage ads. `publisher_identity` is the creator, page, channel, organization, or profile that owns source posts. `post_authorization` is a post-scoped grant when the platform authorizes individual posts instead of, or in addition to, the owning identity.

expires_at.description: Expiration time for the downstream grant, when known.

provider.description: Stable provider or platform namespace, preferably lowercase. Examples: `social.example`, `shortvideo.example`, or a seller-defined namespace. Omit only when the requirement is provider-agnostic, or when an `authorization_url` fully routes the human to the correct provider-specific connection flow.

required_for.description: Concrete AdCP protocol operation names that require this downstream connection. Sellers SHOULD include this in product declarations when the requirement is known ahead of time, and in AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED details when it explains the failed operation. Prefer specific operation names such as `list_creatives`, `sync_creatives`, `create_media_buy`, `get_media_buy_delivery`, or `get_creative_delivery` over broad category labels such as `reporting`.

resource_ref.description: Optional opaque provider-native resource hint, such as a platform account id, profile URL, handle, channel id, post id, or post URL. This is a hint for routing authorization, not proof that authorization exists.

handle.description: Provider-native public handle for the owning identity, when available.

identity_id.description: Provider-native creator, page, channel, organization, or profile id, when safe to disclose.

platform_account_id.description: Provider-native advertiser or business account id, when safe to disclose.

post_id.description: Provider-native post id, when the grant is post-scoped or the failed request referenced a specific post.

post_url.description: Public URL for the referenced post, when available.

profile_url.description: Public URL for the owning identity, when available.

status.description: Current seller-observed state for this downstream connection when known. Product declarations MAY omit status or use `unknown`; AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED details SHOULD use `missing`, `expired`, or `revoked` for the connection that blocked the call.

connection.description: The required connection. Account-independent: `status` is omitted or `unknown`; `resource_ref`, `connection_id`, and `expires_at` MUST be omitted; `required_for`, when present, includes `create_media_buy`.
